title: Ada and the Horizon
premise: Bram Blackwood, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vane Syndicate, takes one last paid job: ferrying supplies upriver to a survey expedition that has gone silent. He finds the camp abandoned, its lead scientist dead, and a teenage girl named Ada—the scientist's daughter—guarding a discovery worth killing for: proof that the Syndicate's flood-control contracts were built on falsified data, dooming the delta towns they claim to protect. Hunted by Syndicate fixers and racing the monsoon, Bram and Ada run the river home carrying evidence they can't safely deliver to any court the Syndicate owns. In the end, Bram chooses justice outside the law, broadcasting the findings from his own storm-chasing rig as the monsoon hits, sacrificing his anonymity—and nearly his life—to give Ada her inheritance: the truth, and a future not owned by anyone.
about_author: Oscar Ashgrove is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade working seasonal expeditions before turning to fiction full-time. He writes adventure stories about people whose debts, literal and moral, finally come due.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Chasing a storm on the plains to earn Syndicate goodwill money, Bram counts what he owes and what he's lost since going invisible seven years ago. The Syndicate offers him a final job: resupply the Halvorsen survey upriver, gone quiet for nine days. Emotional beat: restless dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Quiet Camp
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He arrives at the expedition camp to find it stripped of people, radios smashed, and Dr. Halvorsen buried under a cairn of river stones. In the survey tent he finds a girl, Ada, sixteen, armed with a flare gun and her father's field journals. Emotional beat: grief meeting suspicion; neither trusts the other yet.

chapters.title: What Her Father Found
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She shows Bram the journals: sediment cores proving the levee surveys were faked, meaning the Syndicate-built protections will fail in the coming monsoon. She refuses to leave without the data. Bram realizes why the radio went silent—the Syndicate got there first. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged over shared danger.

chapters.title: Downriver, Fast
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They flee downstream ahead of a Syndicate patrol boat, running the rapids at night with engines muffled. Ada proves herself navigating by her father's hand-drawn charts. They lose the patrol but wreck the propeller shaft. Emotional beat: first flicker of trust earned through competence and courage.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Holed up in an abandoned trading post, Ada reads her father's letters and learns he took Syndicate money knowingly, hoping to expose them from inside—a compromise she must forgive him for. Bram confesses his own debt and how invisibility cost him everyone he loved. Emotional beat: mutual absolution; inheritance reframed as burden and gift.

chapters.title: Fixers at the Ferry
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At a river crossing, Syndicate fixers led by the courteous, terrifying Mr. Sable corner them. Bram trades his boat and his silence for their lives, but Sable recognizes him from seven years ago. They escape on foot into the wetlands. Emotional beat: the past catching up; invisibility officially over.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The monsoon makes early landfall; the wetlands flood around them as they trek toward the last rail junction. Ada watches the first levee fail on a distant ridge exactly as her father predicted—validation and horror at once. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the stakes become the delta's thousands, not just two fugitives.

chapters.title: Every Court They Own
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Reaching the junction town, Bram tries every legal channel—an old journalist friend, a magistrate, a rival contractor—and watches each door close, bought or frightened shut. Sable offers Bram a clean slate in exchange for the cores. Emotional beat: despair crystallizing into clarity; the law is a locked room, so he'll break a window.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. Using his storm-chasing rig's transmitter atop the junction water tower in the teeth of the monsoon, Bram reads the survey data live across every emergency band while Ada guards the ladder against Sable's men. Lightning, wind, gunfire; Sable falls or retreats as the transmission spreads and towns begin evacuating. Emotional beat: sacrifice as triumph; visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: The Horizon, Named
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. Weeks later, investigations bloom, the Syndicate fractures, and the delta rebuilds with honest surveys. Ada publishes her father's work under both their names; Bram, debt voided and name known, stays long enough to teach her to chase storms properly. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled—not property, but truth carried forward together.
